questions.prompt: What does Fern discover the morning after she plants the seed?
choices: The plant is blocking the Hollow Oak doorway.
The seed is still hidden under the soil.
The plant has moved beside the stream.
questions.answer: The plant is blocking the Hollow Oak doorway.
questions.evidenceText: The next morning, the plant had grown so much it filled the Hollow Oak doorway.

questions.prompt: How does Fern solve the growing problem after her spells fail?
choices: She sang to it very softly.
She tried a much stronger spell.
questions.answer: She sang to it very softly.
questions.evidenceText: She did not use a spell. She sang to it, very softly.

questions.prompt: What lesson does Fern learn from calming the giant plant?
choices: Gentle care can work better than forcing a solution.
The slowing spell finally worked after a long delay.
The plant stopped because it had reached full size.
questions.answer: Gentle care can work better than forcing a solution.
questions.rationale: Fern sang to the plant very softly and later says she asked it nicely instead of making it obey; this shows gentle care can work better than forcing a solution.
questions.evidenceText: "I didn't make it do anything," said Fern. "I asked it nicely."

supportingEvidence.evidenceText: She did not use a spell. She sang to it, very softly. She sang the song her mother had taught her about seeds.
